2. Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1 instituted the aforesaid suit for a decree: 

 (a) declaring that the plaintiff is the legally elected Chairman of No. 7, Bangora West Union Parishad on the basis of the Chairman election held on 15.1.84 and the defendant No. I is bound to publish the result in the official. Gazette; 

 3. That the election of the Chairman of the aforesaid Union Parishad was scheduled to be held on 27.12.83 in three Polling Stations, namely, Ward No. 1, Dhanapatikhola Primary School, Ward No. 2, Kodalkata Primary School and Word No. 3 Kurakhal Primary School. Three persons namely, the plaintiff, the defendants No. 6 and 7 contested in the said election. On that date i.e. on 27.12.83 the election of the Ward No. 2 could not be held due to obstruction and interruption which had gone beyond the control of the Presiding Officer and, as such, he stopped the poll in the said Ward and informed the Returning Officer, defendant No 2, accordingly. On 14.1.84 the Returning Officer caused a fresh poll to be held in Ward No. 2 under Rule 29(2) of the Rules. The plaintiff's case is that on counting of total result of the election held on 27.12.83 and 14.1.84 he became elected as he secured the highest number of votes. But as the Election Commission re-fused to publish the result in the official Gazette and defendant No. 2 directed holding of fresh election in the aforesaid Ward No. 2, the plaintiff filed the suit claiming the afore-said reliefs. 

 4. The defendant-petitioner filed the application under Order 7, rule 11 C.P.C. alleging inter alia, that the Presiding Officer and the Returning Officer held the fresh poll illegally in Ward No. 2 on 14 1.84 without any approval of the Election Commission and thereby contravened rule 29(2) (b) of the Rules. The election held on 14.1 84 was no election in the eye of law and, as such, the plaintiff did not acquire any interest or legal character or status to obtain a declaration in the suit as prayed for. The adjourned poll was legally held on 15.4.84 with the approval of the Election Commission in a different Polling Station i.e. Naogaon Primary School centre. The petitioner stated in his application that by telegram dated 11.1.84 the Election Commission directed the Returning Officers not to hold adjourned polls without the approval of the Election Commission and to ensure that approval of the Commission had been obtained by the Returning .Officer before holding of the fresh polls. The said telegram has been quoted in the application. 

 5. On the application filed by the plaintiff for publication of the result of the election held on 14.1.84 in the official Gazette, the Election Commission by its letter dated January 18, 1934 to the Returning Officer stated that the Election Commission had issued instructions to all concerned vide telegram dated 1.1.84.to take prior approval of the Election Commission for holding fresh poll in case of adjourned election. As such, any election if held on 14.1.84 was in violation of rule 29 of the Rules as well as of the instructions of the Election Commission and, therefore the result of such election could not be acceptable for publication in the official Gazette. The Re-turning Officer was directed to appoint a day for a fresh poll in Ward No. 2 for approval of the Election Commission before taking any further action at his end. The Returning Officer informed the Secretary, Election Com-mission on 28.3.84 by wireless message that the adjourned poll of Ward No. 2 of the aforesaid Union Parishad might be held on 15.4 84 and sought approval of the programme. The text of the message has been quoted in the application 

 7. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has submitted orally that pursuant to the election held on 15.4.84 the petitioner obtained the highest number of votes and thus became the successful candidate for Chairmanship but the Gazette in that behalf could not be published because of the injunction order issued by the court in the present suit. It may be mentioned here that upon filing the suit on 7.4.84 the plaintiff prayed for an order of injunction restraining the defendants from holding fresh poll in Ward No. 2 on 15.4.84 or on any subsequent date. By order dated 8.4.84 the learned Munsif asked the defendants to show cause within seven days against the prayer for temporary injunction and in the meantime restrained the defendants from publishing the result of the election of the Union Parishad if the election were held as per schedule i.e on 15.4.84. 

 8. The plaintiff-opposite party opposed the application under section 7, rule 11 C.P.C. by tiling written" objection. He denied the allegations of the defendant-petitioner and asserted that there was no ground for rejection of the plaint and the suit was quite maintain-able under the law. 

 9. The learned Munsiff noticed the cases of the respective parties and observed that the Returning Officer committed an error in not obtaining approval of the Election Com-mission for holding the fresh poll in Ward No. 2 on 14.1.84. He, however, found that there was no illegality in holding the said election in other respects and since the Returning Officer was the authority under the law for convening and holding the fresh poll and further he was a constituent part of the Election Commission. the fresh poll having already been held by him on 14.1.84 and the result having been published he could not Convene the election again He further found that the plaintiff had brought the suit legally and there was not bar under section 9 or the code of Civil Procedure to proceed with the suit. Upon such view of the matter, he rejected the application of the petitioner as already referred to above. 

 10. At the bearing of the Rule, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has sub-mitted that the learned Munsif completely misconceived the grounds upon which the prayer for rejection of the plaint was made and further upon an erroneous view of law and fact rejected petitioner's application. He has submitted that the suit being admittedly one under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the plaint must disclose prima facie that the plaintiff has a legal character to be declared in the suit. In other words, the plaintiff prove that he had a cause of action for the suit. The learned Advocate has submitted that from the plaint and the annexure made thereto it is clear that the fresh poll on 14.1.84 was held by the Returning Officer without the approval of the Election Commission and, as such the said election was a nullity and the plaintiff had acquired no legal character by reason of such election. Thus, there being no cause of action as would be apparent from the plaint, the plaint was liable to he rejected. 

 11. Secondly, he submitted that although apparently the suit was one for declaration and injunction but in effect and substance there was a garbed attack on the election which was to be held on 15 4 84 and which had already taken place The plaintiff it was submitted, resorted to the contrivance of a declaratory suit and thereby sought to avoid section 26 of the Ordinance No. Ll of 1983 which says that no election under this Ordinance shall he called in question except by an election petition under suspect ion (2) It has been argued that section 26 of the Ordinance is a positive bar against the suit of the plaintiff, in as much as, he has made a covert challenge to the election held on 15 4.84. 

 12. A counter affidavit has been tiled on behalf of the opposite party No. I. Appearing for the said opposite party the learned Advocate, Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, has submitted that the plaintiff had obviously a cause of action and it could not be said that the suit was had for absence of cause of anon. He sought to argue that the fresh poll held on 14.1.84 pursuant to which the plaintiff was declared elected was held in accordance with the law and the rules and even if there was any irregularity in not obtaining prior approval of the Election Commission, it could not vitiate the result of the election With regard to the bar of the suit under section 26 of the Ordinance, he has .submitted that the plaintiff's reliefs being what (he are it could not be said that the suit was burro in terms of the aforesaid section. 

 13. Lastly, he has submit that the plaintiff has made allegations of mala fide against the officers of the Election Commission as well as against the defendant petitioner in the conduct of proceedings subsequent to the holding of election on 14.1.84 and, as such, the parties should be allowed to lead evidence in the suit in support of their respective position and the plaint should not be rejected in limine as prayed for. 

 14. It will be apparent from the plaint that the plaintiff has asked for a declaration that he is the legally elected Chairman of the Union Parishad in question on the basis of the election including the fresh poll which was held on 14.1.84. The defendant petitioner has prayed for rejecting the plaint on the ground that even on the facts as disclosed in the plaint it will be seen that the fresh poll held on 14.1.84 was in violation of Rule 29 of the Rules and, as such, there was no election in the eye of law and further that the Election Commission has already caused to be held a fresh poll in Ward No. 2 on 15.4.84 in accordance with law. It is to be seen whether the plaint discloses a prima facie case of the plaintiff having acquired a legal character which may be declared in the suit. In other orders, it has to be seen whether plaintiff has cause of action. 

 15. The Ordinance No. LI of 1983 provides in section 24 that all—elections of Chair-man and elected members of a Union Parishad shall be organised, held conducted by the Election Commission in ordinance with the rules and such rules may provided for, amongst other, the date, time arid place for poll and other matters relating to the conduct of elections. The Rules framed there under show that by Rule 2 has been provided that a fresh poll is to he held by the Returning Officer in case of interruption or obstruction at a particular polling station on a day with the approval of the Election Commission. Admittedly, no approval was obtained by the Returning Officer from the election commission before fixing 14.1 84 for fresh poll This will be evident from annexure. 7 to the plaint where in the Returning Officer in his letter dated 21.1.84 to the Secretary, Election Commission stated that it was assumed that the date of the adjourned poll for the purpose in question would be approved by the Election Commission in due course. The petitioner has refer-red to a telegram dated 11.1.84 addressed to the Returning Officers in his petition and the text of the telegram has been quoted. It appears from the said telegram that the Election Commission before holding of the fresh poll in the instant case instructed the Returning Officers not to hold adjourned polls without the approval of the Election Commission and to ensure that the approval of the Commission had been obtained by the Returning Officers before the holding of the fresh polls. The Returning Officer in his aforesaid letter seems to have taken up the plea that the telegram dated 11.1.84 was received by him on 16.1.84. Be that as it may, it appears from the memo. of the Election Commission dated 18.1.84 annexure-6 to the plaint, that the Election Commission refused to accord approval to the election held on 1 1.1.84 as it was held in violation of rule 29 and the clear instructions of the Election Com-mission and gave further direction to the Returning Officer to appoint day for holding fresh poll of the adjourned election of Ward No 2. It is not disputed that the fresh poll in Ward No. 2 has again been held on 15.4.84 in accordance with the Rule i e. after the date for election was approved by the Election Commission In view of these facts it appears, prima facie, that the plaintiff could not claim himself to be the elected Chairman on the basis of the poll held on 14.1.84 The learned Advocate for the plaintiff referred ale to the facts stated by the plaintiff in his further and better statement which is a port of the plaint. It has been stated there, 74 that not withstanding Rule 29 and the instructions of the Election Commission, at least same adjourned polls were held on 14. 1. 84 elsewhere in the country and the result the elections was duly published in the official Gazette on the basis of such elections, I may be so in a partite case but from the facts of the instant case It is. clear that approval of the Elections, Commission was neither obtained before holding the poll nor the Election Commission accorded its approval subsequent to the holding thereof. On the other hand, the Election Commission insisted that a day be appointed for fresh poll with its approval and cause the fresh poll to be held by the Returning Officer subsequently on 15.4.84 the result of which has not been published because of the injunction order passed in the present suit. I have therefore, come to the conclusion that it is difficult to hold upon the fact disclosed in the plaint that the plaintiff has a prima facie case and for the matter of that a cause of action. 

 16. Secondly, since there has already been a second poll in Ward No 2 under the Rules i.e. with the prior approval of the Election Commission, the plaintiff has of necessity to challenge the said election in, order to gel relief in the present suit. The present suit under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act will not be maintainable if the plaintiff does not impugn the polls that rook place subsequently i.e. on 15 4.R4. In doing so, the plaintiff will inevitably bring himself within the mischief under section 29 of the Ordinance in that it is provided in the said section that no election under that Ordinance shall be called in question except by an election petition under subsection (2). In this view of the matter also it appears to me that the suit in any case will be barred. From the facts as disclosed in the plaint and as transpires from the application of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that the present suit is not only, what the learned Advocate for the petitioner has called it to be a. still-born one but also barred under section of inc Ordinance,
